meta.ogDescription: Napoleon Hill gets the credit and his own foundation reposts it — yet no book, speech or letter has ever been named. What we could and couldn't verify.

answer.label: Attributed to
answer.authorDates: 1883–1970 · American self-help author of “Think and Grow Rich”
answer.sourceLine: Credited to Hill on every major quotation site, and circulated by his own foundation — but no book, speech, letter or article has ever been cited for it. The words “perspiration” and “unbeatable” appear nowhere in the full texts of The Law of Success (1928) or Think and Grow Rich (1937), so the line is consistent with Hill’s themes but pinned to none of his known pages.

source.excerpt: Patience, persistence and perspiration make an unbeatable combination for success.
trail: Neither Quote Investigator ↗ nor Wikiquote ↗ carries this line. Wikiquote’s Hill page lists quotations from The Law of Success (1928) and Think and Grow Rich with page numbers; this sentence is not among them.

We downloaded the OCR text of the 1928 Ralston University Press edition of The Law of Success ↗ and of Think and Grow Rich ↗ from the Internet Archive. Across both, “perspiration” and “unbeatable” each occur zero times — while “patience,” “persistence” and “Carnegie” all occur repeatedly, so the scans are sound.

A-Z Quotes ↗, one of the largest sites carrying the line, cites no Hill book at all: its reference is a 2017 print-on-demand quotation journal. PassItOn ↗ and the rest give the author’s name and nothing else.

The Napoleon Hill Foundation ↗, which publishes and licenses Hill’s work and mails a daily “Thought for the Day” drawn from his writings, posts the line itself ↗ — in a slightly different wording, and without naming a source.
source.excerptNote: There is no fuller passage to show, because no source text has been found. The Napoleon Hill Foundation’s own posting ↗ gives a different wording: “Patience, persistence, and perspiration make for an unbeatable combination for success.”

source.rightsNote: We cannot classify the rights, because we cannot identify the work. If the sentence turned out to come from The Law of Success (1928) it would be public domain in the United States; if it came from Think and Grow Rich (1937) or any of Hill’s later books, courses or columns, it would be in copyright and controlled by the Napoleon Hill Foundation, which asserts rights in Hill’s writings and trademarks his name. Since no source has been established, we assert no status.

author.name: Napoleon Hill
author.heading: Napoleon Hill
author.metaLine: 1883–1970 · American self-help author · “Think and Grow Rich” (1937)
author.bio: Napoleon Hill built the modern success-literature industry out of two enormous books — The Law of Success (1928) and Think and Grow Rich (1937) — both framed as the distilled findings of a twenty-year study of great industrialists commissioned by Andrew Carnegie. Historians have found no evidence for that commission, or for most of Hill’s other biographical claims, and Wikipedia's article describes him as a con man as well as an author. What is not in doubt is the reach: his phrases were promoted relentlessly by his organisation, and they are still promoted daily by the Napoleon Hill Foundation — which is exactly why unsourced aphorisms attach to his name so easily.

cite.sourceCitation: No primary source identified. The wording does not occur in the full texts of Napoleon Hill, The Law of Success (Meriden, CT: Ralston University Press, 1928) or Think and Grow Rich (1937).

misattribution.heading: What the citations actually lead to
misattribution.intro: Hill probably is the right name to have in mind here — but almost everything said about where the line comes from is wrong, and the sourcing that does exist is circular.

items.why: The most common claim online is that the line is from Hill’s 1937 bestseller. It is not. In the complete text of Think and Grow Rich ↗ the words “perspiration” and “unbeatable” never occur once — though “persistence” occurs dozens of times, which is presumably how the association formed.

Same result in Hill’s other flagship. The 1928 Ralston University Press edition ↗ runs to well over a thousand pages and contains neither word. Wikiquote’s Hill page ↗, which cites both books by page number, does not list this sentence at all.

items.who: A-Z Quotes and the aggregator chain
items.why: A-Z Quotes ↗ is unusual in offering any citation — but it points to a 2017 print-on-demand quotation journal, not to Hill. Most sites, including PassItOn ↗, give no source whatever. Every trail ends in another quote collection.

Hill’s own estate circulates the line — and not in the popular wording. Its post ↗ reads “make for an unbeatable combination,” tagged #thinkandgrowrich but with no citation. Two competing wordings and no source text to settle them is the signature of an orally transmitted line.

misattribution.truthLine: Nobody has produced a page. The sentence is Hill-flavoured, Hill-branded and Hill-promoted, but until an edition or a broadcast turns up it is an attribution rather than a citation — and it is definitively not the line from Think and Grow Rich ↗ that people think it is.

context.heading: Why a Hill quote can be famous and sourceless at the same time
lead: Napoleon Hill’s sayings did not spread the way a novelist’s do — page by page, with an edition behind them. They spread as slogans. Quote Investigator’s study of the “conceive … believe … achieve” formula found Hill’s own organisation pushing variants through advertisements, speeches and publications from the early 1950s, with the wording shifting as it went and eventually migrating onto other famous names entirely. A line promoted that way arrives in the world already detached from a page number.

The Foundation still runs a free daily “Thought for the Day” email “based on the writings of Napoleon Hill,” and posts single-sentence Hill quotations to social media without citations. Aggregators harvest those, other aggregators harvest the aggregators, and within a few years the sentence has ten thousand hits and zero sources. That is the exact shape of this one.
context.detailsSummary: Why we stopped short of calling it a fake
detailsBody: Hill wrote far more than the two books everyone searches. The Napoleon Hill Foundation is currently selling a reproduction of Happy Valley Proverbs, a 96-page booklet of “hundreds of powerful insights, guiding principles, and concise proverbs” that Hill prepared for employees of the LeTourneau Company and never released commercially. Material like that — along with his courses, columns and correspondence — is not in any full-text index we can search.

So the negative result is real but bounded: we can say with confidence that this sentence is not in The Law of Success or Think and Grow Rich, and that nobody has ever published a source for it. We cannot say it is not Hill’s. Until someone produces a page, the honest label is “attributed.”
context.pull: Promoted as a slogan, harvested as a quotation, cited by nobody.

sourcesVerified.claim: Wikiquote's Napoleon Hill page cites quotations from The Law of Success (1928) and Think and Grow Rich with page numbers, and does not include "Patience, persistence and perspiration make an unbeatable combination for success."

A-Z Quotes carries the quote credited to Napoleon Hill and gives as its source a 2017 print-on-demand quotation anthology (Mindset Stacking Inspirational Journal, Lulu.com), page 6 — not any work by Hill.
PassItOn carries the exact wording "Patience, persistence and perspiration make an unbeatable combination for success," credited to Napoleon Hill, with no book, date or source given.

The Napoleon Hill Foundation posts the line in the variant wording "Patience, persistence, and perspiration make for an unbeatable combination for success," credited to Napoleon Hill, tagged #thinkandgrowrich, with no source cited.

The Internet Archive hosts a complete, downloadable OCR full text of Think and Grow Rich; fetching that text shows zero occurrences of "perspiration" and zero of "unbeatable," against 89 occurrences of "persistence" and 48 of "Carnegie."

The Internet Archive hosts a scan and downloadable OCR full text of the 1928 Napoleon Hill Law of Success (title page: Ralston University Press, Meriden, Conn., copyright 1928 by Napoleon Hill); that text shows zero occurrences of "perspiration" and zero of "unbeatable."

Wikipedia gives Napoleon Hill's dates as born 26 October 1883 and died 8 November 1970, lists The Law of Success (1928) and Think and Grow Rich (1937), describes him as a self-help author and con man, and states that historians doubt many of his claims including the Andrew Carnegie collaboration.

Quote Investigator's study of the "conceive / believe / achieve" saying documents that Hill's organisation promoted variant wordings through advertisements, speeches and publications from as early as 1952, and that such phrases later migrated onto other famous names.

Matt Novak's Gizmodo investigation (6 December 2016) documents that Hill's biographical claims, including the Carnegie commission behind Think and Grow Rich, are unsupported, and catalogues his fraud and embezzlement record.

The Napoleon Hill Foundation's website offers a free daily "Thought for the Day" email "based on the writings of Napoleon Hill," sells and licenses Hill's books under the registered mark Napoleon Hill, and is currently offering a reproduction of Happy Valley Proverbs, a 96-page booklet Hill prepared for employees of the LeTourneau Company that was never commercially released.
